swap_risks: CRITICAL PACKAGE MISMATCH: LM2903DR uses SOIC-8 (8-pin, D) while LMV331IDBVR uses SOT-23-5 (5-pin, DBV); PCB footprint redesign is mandatory.

CRITICAL PINOUT CONFLICT: Incompatible pin assignments on Pin 1 (OUT_A vs IN_POS), Pin 2 (IN_NEG_A vs VEE), Pin 3 (IN_POS_A vs IN_NEG), Pin 4 (VEE vs OUT), Pin 5 (IN_POS_B vs VCC), Pin 6 (IN_NEG_B vs NONE), Pin 7 (OUT_B vs NONE), Pin 8 (VCC vs NONE). Soldering LMV331IDBVR onto a LM2903DR footprint (or vice versa) without rerouting copper can short VIN/VOUT/GND and permanently damage the board.

CRITICAL SUPPLY VOLTAGE RATING: LMV331IDBVR is limited to 5.5 V max (5.5 V abs max, p.4) whereas LM2903DR supports up to 30 V (36 V abs max, p.4). Installing a 5.5 V CMOS part on a 12 V–24 V rail causes instant breakdown.
HIGH SWITCHING TIMING SHIFT: Propagation delay differs by 4.3x (LM2903DR: 1300 ns p.10 vs LMV331IDBVR: 300 ns p.6); verify overcurrent/zero-crossing trip latency and hysteresis timing.

HIGH INPUT BIAS CURRENT SHIFT: Typical Ib differs by 5000x (LM2903DR: 25000 pA p.10 vs LMV331IDBVR: 5 pA p.6); high-impedance sensor dividers (>100 kΩ) suffer severe Ib·R DC offset error when swapping from CMOS/JFET to bipolar inputs.

CAUTION QUIESCENT CURRENT SHIFT: Supply current per channel differs by 15.4x (LM2903DR: 400 µA/ch p.10 vs LMV331IDBVR: 26 µA/ch p.6); verify battery budget and total power dissipation across all channels.
HIGH ABSOLUTE-MAX SURGE MARGIN: LMV331IDBVR has a lower Vs,abs,max rating (5.5 V, p.4) than LM2903DR (36 V, p.4); verify hot-plug, inductive kickback, and TVS clamp peaks stay safely below 5.5 V.
HIGH THERMAL MARGIN: Package θJA is 51% higher on LMV331IDBVR (LM2903DR: 148.5 °C/W p.5 vs LMV331IDBVR: 224 °C/W p.4); re-check Tj = Ta + Pd × θJA against Tj,max.
HIGH MINIMUM SUPPLY FLOOR: LMV331IDBVR requires Vs,min >= 2.7 V (p.4) vs 2 V on the counterpart; confirm low-battery / brown-out operation still clears the higher floor.
engineering_verdict: LM2903DR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) and LMV331IDBVR (Texas Instruments, SOT-23-5) are NOT drop-in interchangeable (Level 3 PCB Layout / Circuit Change Required) due to package/footprint mismatch; pinout mismatch on Pin 1 (OUT_A vs IN_POS), Pin 2 (IN_NEG_A vs VEE), Pin 3 (IN_POS_A vs IN_NEG), Pin 4 (VEE vs OUT), Pin 5 (IN_POS_B vs VCC), Pin 6 (IN_NEG_B vs NONE), Pin 7 (OUT_B vs NONE), Pin 8 (VCC vs NONE). Specific pin conflicts: Pin 1 (OUT_A vs IN_POS), Pin 2 (IN_NEG_A vs VEE), Pin 3 (IN_POS_A vs IN_NEG), Pin 4 (VEE vs OUT). Signal-chain deltas: propagation delay 1300 ns (p.10) vs 300 ns (p.6), supply ceiling 30 V (p.4) vs 5.5 V (p.4), Vos 7 mV (p.10) vs 7 mV (p.6), Ib 5000x gap (25000 vs 5 pA). Primary bench gotchas to watch: LM2903DR "Extended -40°C to +125°C Upgrade Over LM393DR, But Wider Offset (7 mV / 15 mV Over Temp)" (p.10) and LMV331IDBVR "Reversed U-Pinout SOT-23-5 (Pin 1 = IN+, Pin 4 = OUT) — Incompatible With TLV3201 & TLV7011" (p.3). BOM decision: Choose LM2903DR when supply rails exceed 5.5 V (rated up to 30 V); choose LMV331IDBVR when high-impedance sensors require pA-class input bias (5 pA) or ultra-low supply current (26 µA/ch) is prioritized. Always verify Pin 1 orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.3) and official datasheets on hardware prototypes prior to production.
